attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Close enough to the source, though 'no other hypergrowth markets' (other than gen AI) is a little clearer than the drafter's wording. The line mixes a present observation with an open-ended look forward and gives no threshold.

contract.note: Fair to call this unscoreable. 'Hypergrowth market' has no size or growth threshold, and any test would rest on a cutoff the speaker never gave. 'Nothing else after' has no deadline.

reviews.rationale: This is a sweeping statement with no defined measure of 'hypergrowth' and an open-ended forward element. Scoring it would mean inventing a threshold, and the packet has no evidence items. Not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'sure seems like' hedge on the revenue clause and the 'outside OpenAI' scope. The profit clause is a separate clause with 'certainly', so it is a firm statement.

contract.note: Scoring only the firm profit clause is fair. Leaving chip suppliers out of scope and choosing the 2024 to April 2025 period are evaluator choices, but reasonable ones. The result depends on scope, and on the fact that most firms do not report gen-AI profit separately.

evidence.note: Microsoft reported an AI revenue run rate but no AI-specific profit. This says nothing about profit on gen AI.
Secondhand 2023 report that Midjourney was profitable. It falls before the target period, so it is only a hint of a possible counterexample.

reviews.rationale: No evidence in the packet shows gen-AI profit or loss for any in-scope company during 2024 to April 2025. Microsoft reported revenue only, and the Midjourney report is from 2023. The evidence neither supports nor contradicts the firm profit clause.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: Restores his first-person 'I see no evidence'. The $3B clause sits inside that same framing, so leaving it out is acceptable. 'Marketable' is an evaluative word.

contract.note: Fair. He offers no test of marketability, and he admits some agent products existed. A report of his own perception, judged against an evaluative standard, cannot be settled from the public record.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own announcement of Operator as a limited research preview for Pro users (January 2025). It shows a product existed, not that it was marketable.

reviews.rationale: The claim reports the speaker's own perception and turns on 'marketable', which has no stated test. That Operator existed does not settle it. Not adjudicable.

attribution.note: The framing is a rhetorical question, but Zitron asserts 'the fact it burns billions' in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'No apparent path' keeps the 'does not appear' hedge. The burn clause is firm and checkable.

contract.note: The plain reading (several billion dollars lost or burned in a year) is the ordinary one. Using 2024 is a reasonable period for a present-tense claim made in April 2025. Scoring only the firm clause is fair.

evidence.note: CNBC confirmed company figures showing an expected loss of about $5B in 2024. It is a projection made late in the year, not an audited result, but it is well above the threshold.
Reported $2.5B cash burn in the first half of 2025. Consistent with the claim but outside the 2024 target period.

reviews.rationale: Company figures confirmed by CNBC put OpenAI's 2024 loss at about $5B, comfortably 'billions'. The packet has no counterevidence, and the later 2025 burn figures point the same way. The hedged profit-path clause is not scored.
